analytic.title: A Hard Real-Time Scheduling Algorithm Based on Elastic Model

div.p: Hard real-time systems are time critical systems and widely used in aerospace and other fields. One of the key issues for hard real-time systems is how to increase the CPU utilization while making sure that all tasks would be completed before deadlines. This paper combines EDF and elastic theory and proposes a new algorithm ELTBF to implement the scheduling of hard real-time system with hard periodic tasks and hard aperiodic tasks. Compared with EDF, ELTBF has higher CPU utilization and lower preempt times, and makes sure the number of deadlines missed is zero.

div.head: INTRODUCTION
div.p: A real-time system is a system which is required to complete the task correctly in determinate time [1] . Real-time systems can be divided into hard real-time systems, soft realtime systems and firm real-time systems [2] by the effect when tasks miss their deadlines. A hard real-time system requires that all tasks must be completed before their deadlines, otherwise it will lead to serious consequences. In the process of design and implementation of hard real-time system, the properties of a task must be strictly limited to ensure system time requirements and functional requirements. Therefore, the performance of hard real-time system has been seriously underestimated.

The fixed priority scheduling algorithm is simple and reliable based on the study results of Liu [3] , but the CPU utilization is lower than 100%, so more and more researchers focus their researches on dynamic priority scheduling algorithm. EDF(Earliest Deadline First) algorithm dispatches the tasks' execution order according to their deadlines, the task with the earliest deadline would execute first [4] . In order to improve the efficiency of periodic real-time tasks systems, Chantem proposed a more general real-time task model which allowed to change the periods and deadlines of the tasks [5] . Buttazzo studied the elastic scheduling model [6] which treated the tasks as springs to achieve the rational use of system resources by adjust periods of the tasks [7] .

The scheduling algorithms of soft real-time systems and periodic hard real-time systems had been researched adequately. The research of this paper focuses on hard realtime systems which contain both periodic tasks and aperiodic tasks. This paper proposes a hard real-time scheduling algorithm ELTBF based on elastic model which combines the elastic scheduling theory and EDF to improve the CPU utilization of hard real-time systems effectively.

div.head: II. TASK MODEL
div.p: We assume that the system time is t, and the task set is {T}={T 1 ,T 2 , …, T n }. From our point of view that a task T i is a seven tuple: Ti=<s i , C i , d i , D i , P i , TF i , TB i > s i is the time of T i enters the system; C i is the cost time of T i ; di is the absolute deadline which is a time point T i must be completed before; D i is the relative deadline which is a period between t and di; P i the period of T i (P i would be 0 if T i is a aperiodic task); TF i is the forward time window; TB i is backward time window. T i is shown in "Fig. 1". In preemptive scheduling system, a task may be preempted by higher priority tasks, the actual execution time is uncertain, let the actual execution time of T i is TE i , the waiting time of T i which is preempted is TW i , TE i = TW i + C i .
The following assumptions apply to this work.
The cost time of a task is fixed, which means C i is a constant;
Tasks are independent of each other, and there is no resource conflict between tasks except CPU;
The time of context switching is 0 which can be ignored;
The time of periodic task enter system is 0, s i =0(P i 0); Absolute deadline of periodic task is equals to the end time of current period(di=N•P i , N=1,2,…);

div.head: III. SCHEDULABILITY ANALYSIS
div.p: In a hard real-time system, the task set is composed of a periodic task set and an aperiodic task set.

Definition 3. Periodic Task. A periodic task is completed once in a fixed period. A periodic task is required to assure the start time and finish time of task are within the period range, as long as the condition is satisfied, two tasks can be defined as periodic tasks even the time difference between the two start time is longer than period. A periodic task is shown in "Fig. 2". Within the hyperperiod, a periodic task set is schedulable if the sum of periodic tasks' cost time less than the hyperperiod.

Let the hyperperiod of periodic task set {T p } as HP T , the task model this paper proposed meet the requirement that relative deadline is shorter than period of the task according to [8]. Within the hyperperiod, the sum of a periodic task set's cost time is as below:
The utilization of the periodic task set {T P } is less than 1, hence, {T P } is schedulable.

In real-time system, a periodic task set is schedulable is the certainly need insufficiency condition of a task set is schedulable. Therefore, a task set would be unschedulable when aperiodic tasks enter the system with the periodic task set only. The unschedulable task set may lead to serious consequence of hard real-time system.

If the periodic task set of a task set is schedulable, and the sum of aperiodic tasks' cost time is less than the difference between the hyperperiod of the task set and the sum of periodic tasks' cost time, the task set is schedulable.

We should estimate and measure all tasks' cost time when we design a real-time system, and adjust the periods of task set reasonably to assure the schedulability.

div.head: A. Elastic Model
div.p: The elastic scheduling model was proposed by Buttazzo et al. [6] . This model treats a task in real-time system as a spring which is flexible. The periods of the tasks can be changed within a time range, and the results of executing the tasks are available [7] . A task set of a real-time system can be treated as a spring system with a set of connected springs, when the spring system is forced, each spring of the system would undertake a part of the force to ensure the system's stability. A spring system is shown in "Fig. 4" In traditional elastic model of task set, when the system is affected by a force, periods of the tasks would be changed to adjust the force. Assume that there are three tasks T 1 , T 2 , T 3 in a task set which is schedulable, a new task T 4 would make the utilization more than 1 when it enters the system. The traditional elastic model would extend the periods of T 1 , T 2 and T 3 to make the utilization of the new system less than 1 to make sure the schedulability of the new task set. However, the deadline of a periodic task is the end edge of the period, it would lead the actual finish time later than the theoretical deadline of a task. Therefore, the traditional elastic model commonly used on soft real-time system.
In this paper, the traditional elastic model is improved to adjust the stringent requirements of task deadline for hard realtime system.

We divided a periodic task into three parts: execute time, forward time window and backward time window. Forward time window is used to adjust the start time of a task in its period to lower the times of preemption, backward time window is the rest time of a period after task running which is used to be allocated to aperiodic tasks. The elastic model is shown in "Fig. 5". An aperiodic task can be treated as a spring with the same structure of a periodic task, but aperiodic task's forward time window is used to adjust the current schedule state waiting for higher priority tasks to ensure the execution of more urgent tasks which is different from periodic task. The frontier of aperiodic task's forward time window is the time the task enters the system, and the tailing edge of forward time window is the time the task get CPU and start running. The backward time window is the rest time after aperiodic task running before its deadline, the rest time can be returned to system to be allocated to other tasks for running.

div.head: B. Elastic Least Backward Time Window First Scheduling
div.p: We focus on a preemptive hard real-time scheduling system in this paper, the basis of a preemption is task priority. The effect of task priority to system is researched adequately [1][3][9] [10] , fixed priority is simple and reliable, but utilization of fixed priority scheduling system is lower, dynamic priority can hold a high utilization of resource which even is 100%, such as EDF algorithm [3] . We are under the perspective of the urgency of the task to improve EDF algorithm in this paper. We use backward time window TB i to be the priority of a task, the less value of TB i means the closer to deadline and the more urgency of the task.

Based on the model described above, the scheduling algorithm would analysis the schedulability of task set first, then adjust task set using elastic theory to make the highest priority task running first. The details of the algorithm are shown in "Fig. 6" and "Fig. 7" For example, there is a task set {T} shown in "Table I". There are 4 tasks in {T}, T 1 , T 2 and T 3 are periodic tasks, these three tasks enter the system at time 0, the periods are 2, 4 and 5 time units, and the cost time are all 1 time unit. T 4 is an aperiodic task which enters at time 10 and T 4 must be completed before time 30. The task set would be executed in different sequences depending on different scheduling algorithms. The scheduling results of the task set are shown in "Fig. 8" using EDF and "Fig. 9" using ELTBF.

div.head: C. Test Results
div.p: The ELTBF algorithm we proposed in this paper combines the elastic theory and EDF algorithm, we select TB to be the priority which used to adjust the time property of task set for elastic scheduling to increase the utilization on the base of meeting hard real-time requirements. To evaluate the performance of the improved algorithm, we use CPU utilization, preempt times and deadline miss number to compare the performance difference between ELTBF and EDF.

Let the number of periodic tasks for three tests are 10, 20 and 30, the period and cost time of each task is produced randomly in the range of 10 to 100 time units, and the deadline of each periodic task is the tailing edge of the period. Each test executes for 1000 time units with 10 aperiodic tasks produced randomly, and there is no overlap between the tasks. After schedulability analysis of the three task sets, ELTBF and EDF are used to be tested, the results are shown below From "Table II", we can see that the CPU utilization of ELTBF is higher than EDF. The utilizations of two algorithms are same when analyzing the schedulability before system start running, but there are some tasks missing their deadlines when EDF scheduling, so the utilization became lower.

"Table III" shows the preempting number of two algorithms, we can see that the number of ELTBF is less than EDF by 30%~50%, this is because of the function of forward time window. ELTBF would larger the value of TF of lower priority tasks which are waiting for running to delay the start running time to ensure the decrease of preempt number.

The "Table IV" shows there is no deadline miss in ELTBF algorithm, with EDF happens 2, 5 and 13 times. We can conclude that the performance of ELTBF is higher than EDF, and ELTBF is more suitable for hard real-time system.

div.head: V. SUMMARY
div.p: While designing a hard real-time system, it's necessary to increase the CPU utilization while making the assurance of all tasks would be completed before their deadlines. This paper proposed a new algorithm named ELTBF based on EDF to improve the shortage that the deadline miss number is more than 0 of EDF and decrease the preempt times. The test results show that improved algorithm implement 0 deadline miss and lower preempting times on the base of high CPU utilization.
